title: Music & Instruments of the World
strapline: Djembe, maracas, bells and gongs — the world has a thousand ways to make music.
intent: Playing and hearing instruments from many cultures opens children's ears to the rich variety of music across the world.
Exploring how different instruments make sound builds real knowledge of pitch, rhythm, beat and how things work.
Drumming, shaking and strumming is joyful whole-body, fine-motor and expressive play.
Hearing music from around the world honours children's heritages and widens their sense of belonging.
Making music together builds turn-taking, listening and playing as part of a group.
implementation: Offer a range of real or made instruments from different cultures — a djembe, maracas, bells, a rainstick, finger cymbals — to explore freely.
Play music from around the world and invite children to move, listen and join in with their own instruments.
Wonder together about the sounds: 'How does this one make its sound? Is it high or low, fast or slow?'
Feed in vocabulary lightly — loud and quiet, fast and slow, beat and rhythm, and instrument names.
Invite families to share a song, a rhythm or an instrument from their own culture.
Follow the children — some will drum for the joy of it, others will lead a whole-group band.
key_questions: How does this instrument make its sound?
Is this music fast or slow, loud or quiet?
Can you copy the rhythm I play, then make one for me?
Which instrument do you like best — why?
What music does your family like to listen to?

impact.text: Children explore instruments and experiment with rhythm, volume and pitch.
Children copy and create rhythms and patterns of sound.
Children learn about instruments and music from different cultures.
Children play music together, listening and taking turns in a group.
Children use sound words — loud, quiet, fast, slow — as they play.

enhancements: A world-instruments basket — djembe, claves, bells, rainstick, finger cymbals — to explore.
Recordings of music from many countries for moving and listening.
A make-your-own-instrument table with shakers, drums and strummers.
A family-shared song or rhythm learned and performed together.
A loud-and-quiet, fast-and-slow conducting game for the whole group.

playing_exploring: Children explore every instrument for the joy of the sounds they make.
They move and respond to music from around the world with their whole bodies.
active_learning: Children keep working at a rhythm until they can play it.
They play as part of a group, listening and holding their part.
creating_thinking: Children work out how each instrument makes its sound.
They invent rhythms and patterns and lead others in playing them.
